items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: And in this particular band we had Edward Inge, did you ever hear, he used to play with Don Redmond.

ctx.x: I think Audis Starks was on there, Clamondon and Saxe.

So we came back, Pay Night and Padlock was on the place. I know 5250 was paying us. I didn't really get that money, I just said married to. And so then I went and joined Arthur Sims in Milwaukee at the Wisconsin Roof. And so after about a year with Arthur, Arthur caught pneumonia in August and died. So then a fellow who is now a physician, Arthur Albright, he was the oldest man in the band. He was a guitar player and banjoist. So he was taking over the band and then he left to go to Meharry to study medicine.…

items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: Later on they played with Don Redmond, Shirley Clay, nice trumpet player.

ctx.x: I talked to him the other day.

He had a studio right there at 36th Estate you know. He had the band in Milwaukee, the Wisconsin roof, before Sims had it. He comes or he leaves there and goes to Savoy. That's when Sims goes on in there and when Sims is about a year or so I go in there with Sims. But he had a good band, he had a good band, he had good Harmon's Bremen. He had Riverview. He and Cook, those fellas, they had some of the best jobs to be had. McGuire's down on Clark Street. I follow Roy and Dutray and him all around. And I get into…
Yeah, he's from Denver but he's been there.
